**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 6, §6.4. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

Summary statistics describe central tendency and variability; independence asks whether observing one variable changes beliefs about another. These are different tasks.

## Formal relationship

$$
\bar y=\frac1n\sum_i y_i,\quad s_y^2=\frac1{n-1}\sum_i(y_i-\bar y)^2,\quad X\perp Y\iff P(X,Y)=P(X)P(Y)
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

Our recorded times sum to 87 minutes, so their mean is 14.5 minutes. The deviation of the 7-minute observation from the mean is -7.5. Covariance summarises co-variation; zero covariance alone does not generally establish independence.

## Interpretation and limitations

Independence is about the full joint distribution, not whether two vectors are linearly independent. Sample estimates are noisy and depend on data collection.

## Explain it yourself

Compute the empirical mean item count. Why does a higher distance-time correlation not prove distance causes delay?
